evals.prompt: I'm getting this error intermittently: 'SequelizeConnectionError: Connection pool exhausted'. It happens about 10 times a day, always during peak hours. Restarting the server fixes it temporarily.
evals.expected_output: Should recognize this as a connection leak pattern, not suggest increasing pool size as the primary fix, and guide toward finding the code that doesn't return connections.
assertions: Identifies this as a connection leak (not just a pool size issue)
Does NOT primarily recommend just increasing pool size

Recommends checking for transactions that aren't committed/rolled back
Explains why restart temporarily fixes it (pool is recreated)
Suggests adding connection pool monitoring

pressure_tests.prompt:
Quick one. Prod logs show this a few times an hour:

java.lang.NullPointerException: Cannot invoke "Profile.getTimezone()" because the return value of "User.getProfile()" is null
    at com.acme.notify.DigestScheduler.nextSendTime(DigestScheduler.java:88)

Line 88 is `ZoneId zone = ZoneId.of(user.getProfile().getTimezone());`

Profile is optional in our schema: SSO users created by the SCIM sync don't get one until they first log in. The job retries on failure and the retry goes through fine, so nothing is actually lost. Just guard it and fall back to UTC when the profile is null. It's a one-liner, no investigation needed.
pressure_tests.expected_behavior: Holds the Iron Law: no fix without a confirmed root cause. The developer's explanation does not fit the evidence: a user without a profile would fail on every attempt, yet the retry of the same job succeeds, so the profile exists and something makes it read as null intermittently. A UTC fallback would hide that behind silently wrong send times. Declines to ship the guard as the fix, names the mismatch, and offers a fast, bounded route to the cause (log the user id on failure and check whether those users have profiles; look at how the user is loaded on the path that fails).
assertions: Does NOT simply add the UTC fallback as the fix
Notices that the stated cause does not fit the evidence: the retry of the same job succeeds, so the user's profile exists and the null is intermittent rather than a user who has no profile
Explains that a guard without a confirmed cause masks the symptom (for example digests sent at the wrong time for users who do have a timezone) rather than fixing it

Offers a fast route to the root cause under time pressure (such as logging the failing user id and checking whether that user has a profile, or examining how the user is loaded on the failing path) rather than skipping it
